title: Are Fake Citations a Form of Reward Hacking? A Pre-Registered Study of Post-Training and Citation Cues
abstract: arXiv:2611.01313v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Post-trained language models fabricate citations at high rates. We ask whether that is reward hacking: scoring well on a proxy for scholarship while doing worse on what it stands for. We ran four pre-registered experiments on 900 frozen questions (US federal case law, computationally adjacent scientific literature, and medical literature) across twelve open-weights checkpoints covering four post-training stages of three model families, then refit on fifteen. The clearest result holds the weights fixed and changes only the prompt. Asking for citations raises fabrication sharply in post-trained checkpoints and not in base ones: a 47.8-point interaction on twelve checkpoints (Holm-adjusted p = 2e-34) and 41.5 points on fifteen, in all three domains. A length-matched control separates the citation cue from a demand for a longer answer, so the effect is specific to citations, not verbosity. Post-training also raises fabrication overall, fro

translated_title: 虚假引用是奖励黑客行为的一种形式吗？关于后训练与引用线索的预注册研究
translated_abstract: 后训练的语言模型会以很高的频率伪造引用。我们探究这是否属于奖励黑客行为：即在学术研究能力的代理指标上得分很高，却在代理指标所代表的真实能力上表现更差。我们在900个固定问题上开展了四项预注册实验（涵盖美国联邦判例法、计算相关科学文献和医学文献），涉及三个模型家族四个后训练阶段的十二个开源权重检查点，随后又在十五个检查点上重新拟合验证。最清晰的结论来自保持权重固定、仅改变提示词的实验：要求提供引用会大幅提高后训练检查点的伪造率，而对基础模型没有影响——在十二个检查点上交互效应达47.8个百分点（经Holm校正的p = 2e-34），在十五个检查点上为41.5个百分点，且在所有三个领域中均成立。一个长度匹配的对照实验将引用线索与“要求更长的回答”区分开来，说明该效应是引用特有的，而非回答冗长所致。后训练还在整体上提高了伪造率……
tldr: 四项预注册实验表明，要求提供引用会显著提高后训练模型（而非基础模型）伪造引用的比率，且该效应在三个领域均成立，说明虚假引用是后训练模型奖励黑客行为的一种形式。
en_tdlr: Through four pre-registered experiments across three domains, the study finds that requesting citations sharply increases fabrication in post-trained models but not base models, indicating that fake citations are a form of reward hacking.
